Robot Tutorial illustrations

Explore the geometry, controls, and configuration behind the tutorial's drivers. Follow the chapter links for explanations and exercises, or click an image to enlarge it.

Architecture / Components and lifecycle

The architecture diagrams use the same visual language as the tutorial. Their editable SVG sources live in the shared documentation image folder.

01 / Heading is not position

A car can point along the road while being far from its centerline, or sit on the centerline while facing the wrong direction. Steering must account for both errors.

02 / Centerline distance is not clearance

A barrier at the road edge can block the body even when the car's center is near the middle. Three distinct poses show contact, separation, and room to turn. Chapter 2 also includes a close-up of a body corner near the barrier, shown below.

03 / Choose a useful direction

04 / Look at the corner, not just the heading

Chapter 3 / Choose your speed

Corner radius, grip, braking distance, and gearing determine how quickly the car can approach a bend. Chapter 3 connects these measurements to the speed controller.

Chapter 3 / Optional deeper reading

Chapter 4 / Look ahead and follow a path

The centerline distance, target direction, car heading, and driven path have different roles. These diagrams use explicit geometric constructions; the paths are not simulator traces. Read Chapter 4 for the driving experiments.

Chapter 5 / Share the road

Measure the space around both cars and follow a manoeuvre from following through passing and returning. Read Chapter 5 for the traffic-planning rules and racing exercises.

Chapter 6 / Complete the driver

Route construction, service capture, and coordinated controls come together in Chapter 6. The spline plots show how endpoint positions and slopes shape the pit route.
